description.narrative:
Project 1 of the Road Network Investment Program aims to develop an adequate, efficient, safe, and sustainable road network, linking the country domestically and internationally.
Project 1 has four components: (i) construction of about 22.1 km of a new expressway between Masalli and Astara on the southern corridor, (ii) rehabilitation of local roads in the project area and along East-West highway, (iii) installation of four vehicle weighing stations in selected locations, and (iv) project support and capacity building for road network management.

description.narrative: An efficient, safe, and sustainable southern road corridor from Baku.

5% increase in passenger traffic by 2017 (Baseline: 10,892 million passenger-km in 2005). Progress/Status: Passenger traffic is growing in general on account of improved road network and road condition. Target already reached. 2010 figure recorded at 16,633 million passenger-km. Further assessment will be made after the project's physical completion in 2017. Data Source: ARS surveys; Road subsector budget and expenditure records; MFF Progress and completion reports Actual value:

2% reduction in road traffic accidents by 2017 (Baseline: 3,179 in 2005). Progress/Status: Road safety is improving in general. Target already reached. 2011 figure is at 2,890 number of accidents. It is expected that at least six months prior to the opening for operation of the project road, MOT will develop implementation plan, acceptable to ADB, for ensuring appropriate safety enforcement measures on the project road and shall cause ARS to monitor the accident rate and traffic volume after commencement of the operation of the project road. Assessment will be made after the completion of project by 2017. Data Source: ARS surveys; Road subsector budget and expenditure records; MFF Progress and completion reports Actual value:

Increased funding for road maintenance to at least $100 million in 2017 (Baseline: $55 million in 2006). Progress/Status: Budget allocation for road maintenance is growing. Target already reached. 2011 figure is at $200 million. It is anticipated that ARS will develop such a road maintenance plan for the period up to 2017. Data Source: ARS surveys; Road subsector budget and expenditure records; MFF Progress and completion reports Actual value:

10% increase in freight traffic by 2017 (Baseline: 7,536 million ton-km in 2005). Progress/Status: Freight traffic is growing in general on account of improved road network and road condition. Target already reached. 2010 figure recorded at 11,325 million ton-km. Further assessment of freight trafic will be made after the project's physical completion in 2017.
